title: Hearing the verses, he says: old stories.
subtitle: Dismissing what you do not want to face
then: Ibn Kathir says whenever this man heard Allah's words from the Messenger ﷺ, he {trap}denied them and thought ill of them{/trap}, claiming they were gathered from the books of earlier peoples. The same line appears in other surahs.
now: A reminder comes up in the family group chat and you scroll past: "heard it before." A talk at the masjid feels old-fashioned. {idea}Calling something old is an easy way to never let it reach you.{/idea}
old: I have heard all this before. It is nothing new.
new: A verse I know by heart can still be speaking to me today.
try: Read one short verse you know well, slowly, as if hearing it for the first time.

title: No. What they earned has rusted over their hearts.
subtitle: Why truth stopped getting through
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith from Abu Hurayrah: when a servant sins, a black spot appears in his heart. {reward}If he repents, his heart is polished clean.{/reward} {trap}If he returns, it grows until it covers the heart.{/trap}
now: A phone screen with years of fingerprints. You do not notice the smudge until you hold it to the light. {idea}One honest istighfar wipes a spot before it hardens.{/idea}
old: One more slip will not change anything about me.
new: Each sin leaves a mark, and each repentance can wipe one clean.
try: Before sleeping tonight, say astaghfirullah slowly for one specific thing.

title: That Day, they are screened from their Lord.
subtitle: The loss beneath every other loss
then: Right after the covered heart comes the veil. Ibn Kathir reports Imam Ash-Shafi'i saying that {reward}this verse is proof that the believers will see Allah on that Day{/reward}, since only the deniers are screened.
now: You sit in the same room as someone you love but are both on your phones. Close, yet shut out. {idea}What you let cover your heart now shapes what you will see later.{/idea}
old: The worst thing about the Hereafter would be the pain.
new: The deepest loss is being kept from seeing my Lord.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to let you see Him on that Day.

title: Then they enter the Fire they denied.
subtitle: The end of the denier's road
then: The surah lays out the steps plainly: a sealed record, a covered heart, a veil, and {trap}then the Fire{/trap}. It was spoken to Makkans who were laughing at the warning while there was still time.
now: A sat-nav keeps saying "turn around when possible." You can ignore it for miles, but each exit is a chance. {reward}Every day you are alive is an exit off this road.{/reward}
old: Warnings about the Fire are for other kinds of people.
new: The warning is a mercy because it comes while I can still turn.
try: Name one thing you keep putting off changing. Take the first small step today.

title: This is what you used to call a lie.
subtitle: The moment denial meets the fact
then: The same people who said {trap}legends of the former peoples{/trap} in verse 13 now hear it turned back: this is the very thing you denied. The surah closes the loop on their own words.
now: The warning light on the car dashboard you kept ignoring, until the breakdown. The doctor's advice you laughed off, until the test results. {idea}Better to believe the warning before it becomes the event.{/idea}
old: I will take it seriously if it ever actually happens.
new: By the time it happens, it is too late to start believing it.
try: Act on one reminder today that you have been brushing off.

title: No. The record of the righteous rises to Illiyyin.
subtitle: The opposite file, the opposite place
then: Ibn Kathir says the righteous are in the opposite situation to the wicked. Illiyyin is taken from the word for {reward}highness{/reward}. Ibn Abbas said it means Paradise; others placed it in the seventh heaven.
now: The quiet charity, the night you held your tongue, the parent you visited after a long shift. {reward}None of it vanished. It went up.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds probably do not add up to much.
new: The good I do is filed in a high place, and it keeps rising.
try: Do one hidden good deed today that only Allah will know about.

title: And what will make you know what Illiyyin is?
subtitle: The same question, now about honour
then: The same question that made Sijjin heavy now makes Illiyyin grand. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah magnifies its affair and extols its matter{/reward} by asking it.
now: You picture the dream job or the dream house and it is already small next to the real thing. {idea}What Allah has prepared is bigger than any picture you can hold.{/idea}
old: I have a rough idea of what reward looks like.
new: The reward is greater than anything I can picture, so it is worth reaching for.
try: Spend one minute today imagining the best of Paradise, then thank Allah for the hope.

title: Their place too is written in a sealed register.
subtitle: Good deeds are recorded just as firmly
then: The exact phrase from verse 9 returns, "a register inscribed." Ibn Kathir says it affirms {reward}what will be written for the righteous{/reward}. The firmness that warned the wicked now comforts the good.
now: Your boss forgot the extra project you did. Your kids will not remember the nights you stayed up. {reward}The register does not forget.{/reward}
old: If nobody saw it, it might as well not have happened.
new: Every good deed is written firmly, whether or not anyone noticed.
try: Recall one good thing you did that no one thanked you for. Let that be enough.

title: Those brought near bear witness to it.
subtitle: An honoured record with honoured witnesses
then: Qatadah said those brought near are the angels. Ibn Abbas said {reward}those nearest to Allah in each heaven will witness it{/reward}. The record of the righteous is seen and honoured.
now: You hold back from posting the volunteer photo and feel a small sting nobody saw it. {idea}Someone did. A better audience than any feed.{/idea}
old: Good deeds feel wasted if no one sees them.
new: My good is witnessed by those near to Allah, which is better than any audience here.
try: Do one good deed today and tell no one about it.

title: The righteous will be in delight.
subtitle: Where the honest scale finally leads
then: Ibn Kathir says the righteous will be in {reward}eternal pleasure and gardens of comprehensive bounties{/reward}. It answers the cheaters at the start of the surah: honesty is not a loss.
now: You turned down the side deal that would have paid for a holiday. You told the customer about the defect. {reward}It felt like losing at the time.{/reward} The verse says it was not.
old: Being honest in business means I will always earn less.
new: Honesty leads to a delight that no shortcut can buy.
try: Next time honesty costs you a little today, say alhamdulillah and keep going.

title: On raised couches, they look.
subtitle: At rest, and given sight
then: Ibn Kathir gives two meanings: they look at the kingdom and bounties Allah gave them, or {reward}they look at Allah, the Mighty and Sublime{/reward}. Either way it is the opposite of the veil in verse 15.
now: After a long week you finally sit down and just look out the window, no rush. {reward}Imagine that rest, but forever, and with the best view there is.{/reward}
old: Rest is something I will never really get.
new: A rest is coming where I sit at ease and see what matters most.
try: Take five quiet minutes today to sit, look at something Allah made, and say subhanAllah.

title: You will see the glow of delight on their faces.
subtitle: Joy that shows from the inside
then: Ibn Kathir says you will notice a {reward}glow of delight in their faces{/reward}, a sign of happiness, composure and honour from the great bounty they are in.
now: You can tell when someone is truly happy: a grandparent holding a new baby, a friend just out of hospital. {reward}No filter needed.{/reward} That is the kind of face this verse describes.
old: Happiness is something you show, even if you do not feel it.
new: Real delight shines out without trying.
try: Smile at one person today and mean it.
